spec: Clips adapter and trims low-quality read ends to keep synthetic sequence and miscalled bases out of the assembly.
note: bbduk answers every `clean_reads` target today. fastp is the closer match to KBase's canonical trimmomatic, it is already written, and it reports its own before/after stats -- which bbduk does not. Optional.

spec: Measures per-base quality, GC distribution, duplication and adapter content of a short-read library. Catches a failed run before it is assembled.
note: `assembly/seqkit_reads.py` produces `sequences::read_qc_stats`, which is what downstream consumes. What is missing is the human-facing report, and both transforms that produce one are already written and sitting in `_disabled/` with their product types already declared. Optional: nothing is blocked without them.

spec: Measures the read length and quality distribution of a long-read run. Confirms the reads are long enough to span the repeats they were sequenced for.
note: `assembly/seqkit_reads.py` produces `sequences::read_qc_stats`, which is what downstream consumes. What is missing is the human-facing report, and both transforms that produce one are already written and sitting in `_disabled/` with their product types already declared. Optional: nothing is blocked without them.

spec: Drops contigs below a length or coverage threshold so binning reads composition and coverage from contigs long enough to carry a stable signal.
note: `select_chromosomal_contigs.py` filters, but only a hifiasm_meta assembly, and only by circularity. Length and coverage fractionation is generic and every metagenomics workflow does it before binning.

spec: Corrects residual base errors in a long-read assembly against accurate short reads. Stops homopolymer indels frameshifting real genes out of the annotation.
note: Zero narrative copies on the KBase side, and proposed anyway: short-read polishing of a long-read assembly is the missing step in `isolate_assembly_from_long_reads`, which is a shipped template.

spec: Names every protein an ORF caller found, against bakta's curated hierarchy of identical proteins, then protein clusters, then HMMs. Turns a set of unlabelled reading frames into a genome you can ask questions of.
note: `bakta_proteins`, a separate entry point beside `bakta` in the pinned 1.11.0 image, verified present and taking a protein FASTA -- so the input is ORF calls, as asked. It writes five files and all five are declared: `.tsv` is the per-ORF hit table, `.inference.tsv` the evidence behind each call, and those two are the hit/definition pair `gpr_4lane` uses. `.hypotheticals.tsv` carries the Pfam and physicochemical analysis of what stayed unnamed, which is a real result rather than a leftover.

spec: Calls tRNA, rRNA, ncRNA, tmRNA, CRISPR arrays and oriC on an assembly. These are the features an ORF caller cannot see, and they are what makes a genome record complete rather than a list of proteins.
note: The transform ships and runs at scale -- 2,462 samples and 46 GB in cyanoverse's `W06rU63X`. It declares 2 of the 12 files bakta writes. Three of the other ten are worth declaring: `.gbff` is the annotated genome record and is the interchange format everything downstream of `annotate` reads, `.ffn` carries the non-coding feature sequences, `.txt` is the per-genome summary. The remaining seven are empty or duplicate the input under `--skip-cds`.

spec: Searches a chosen query set against a chosen subject. Answers whether a named gene is present in a given genome, which a fixed reference database cannot.
note: Generalises `amplicon/blast_map_asvs.py`, which already runs makeblastdb then blastn over a query and a subject and differs only in being typed to `amplicon::asv_seqs` and `amplicon::asv_contig_map`. Same finding as the ecology lane -- the capability ships, locked to one namespace.

spec: Tests which GO terms occur in a selected gene set more often than the annotated genome background gives. Turns several hundred differentially expressed genes into a statement about function.
note: interproscan already emits the GO terms. The gene set is whatever selected the genes -- a DE result, a bin, a blast hit list.

spec: Reshapes per-sample kraken reports into one sample-by-taxon count table, the form every diversity, ordination and differential abundance method requires.
note: Produces the type the ecology lane already reads, rather than a new one. A kraken2 report and an ASV table are the same shape: samples by taxa, counts.

spec: Infers a tree from the concatenated marker protein alignment GTDB-Tk already builds. Resolves relationships too distant for whole-genome similarity to measure.
note: Yes, it is the same tool. `taxonomy/gtdbtk.py` runs `classify_wf`, which already performs identify and align, then keeps only `classify/*summary.tsv` -- the concatenated marker MSA it wrote is discarded. Two changes rather than a new pipeline: declare `gtdbtk_msa` as a product of the transform that already writes it, and add `gtdbtk infer` over that MSA for the tree.

spec: Partitions pangenome families into core, accessory and unique with their functions attached. The accessory fraction is where a lifestyle difference between strains shows.
note: A readout on an existing product. No new tool.

spec: Aligns homologous sequences so each column holds one ancestral position, the precondition for any tree, conservation score or selection test.
note: `gtdbtk_de_novo` covers the marker case, which is what the tree needs. A bare alignment of a user's own sequences is a different job and a one-tool transform.

spec: Resolves a gene-to-reaction table into a mass-balanced network. Mass balance is what makes flux prediction possible from reaction content.
note: The metasmith route from a genome to reaction content is the GPR table, which `fabfos/gpr_4lane.py` and `gpr_7lane.py` already build from ORFs and annotations. This closes it into a model, reusing `fba_scaffold.parse_mnx_equation` and `load_reac_prop` rather than adding a ModelSEED reconstruction lane beside them.

spec: Fetches a manually curated model from BiGG by accession. A curated biomass equation and curated gene-protein-reaction rules are the sound baseline to measure a draft reconstruction against.
note: Source named explicitly: BiGG, `http://bigg.ucsd.edu/static/models/<id>.json`, pinned by model id. The id is the accession, the way `ncbi::assembly_accession` is, so the transform matches `getNcbiAssembly.py` in shape. fabfos's `vs_gem/bridge.py` holds the per-host model set this generalises.

spec: Solves for the flux distribution that maximises biomass under mass balance and the medium's uptake limits. Given a conditions table it solves one row per medium and knockout, which predicts gene essentiality and scores the model against observed growth.
note: `ecspr::conditions` is optional and it is what absorbs `predict_phenotype`: a conditions table is one row per medium and mask, which is a KBase PhenotypeSet in this repository's own idiom. Given terminals it solves once, given conditions it solves every row -- the same shape ecspr's probes already use, deliberately.

spec: Adds the smallest set of universal reactions that lets the model grow on a medium, and labels every one it adds. Without it a missing annotation returns zero growth, which reads as a biological result.
note: `fba_scaffold.build_scaffold` already inserts non-native reactions from the MetaNetX universe into a cobra model, creating the metabolites they need and guarding the unmappable ones. That is gapfilling, written and exercised. The transform is that function with the medium as the feasibility target rather than a benchmark panel.

spec: Places RNA-seq reads on a bacterial reference without splitting a read across a gap. A bacterial transcript is colinear with the genome, so a spliced aligner invents introns to raise its own score.
note: Pairs with the new `bakta.py`: assembly -> bakta gff -> bowtie2 -> counts is the bacterial RNA-seq chain, and every step but this one and the next would then exist.

spec: Counts the reads falling inside each feature the annotation names. Produces the count table differential expression is defined on.
note: `stringtie -e -G` against the bakta GFF, which is `stringtie_quant.py` with a bacterial bam and a bacterial annotation in place of a STAR bam and a braker merged GTF. It produces the existing `stringtie_quant_gtf`, so `stringtie_count_matrix.py`, `deseq2.py` and `pydeseq2.py` serve it unchanged and no subread environment is needed.

spec: Groups genes whose expression moves together across conditions. Recovers the operon and the regulon, which per-gene testing reports as unrelated hits.
note: The clustering script already ships as a `lib::` resource for the pangenome heatmap. KBase's four apps here are hierarchical, k-means, WGCNA and an estimate of k -- one transform with a method knob, not four.

spec: Reports mapping rate, depth and insert size for an alignment. Separates a wrong reference from a wrong sample from a sample that is simply quiet.
note: Mapping rate, depth and insert size. Four narrative copies on the KBase side, and it is the readout every alignment in this library currently has no way to report.

spec: Calls the positions where aligned reads disagree with the reference. Recovers the strain variation an assembly consensus collapses to one base.
note: One KBase app, one narrative copy. A specific tool with a specific job, and last in the order.
